Automatic landmarking of a batch of photographs (no clicks)

Source: R/batch_landmarks.R
batch_landmarks.Rd

Runs the fully automatic ml-morph chain on every photograph of a folder, without opening them: the GLOBAL network (mlmorph_run_global/model.onnx) finds the snout (LM1), the caudal-fin basis (LM2) and the dorsal side on the whole photograph (then on a zoomed crop of the fish), and the neural-network model of the canonical frame (mlmorph_run_cnn/model.onnx) places the other landmarks. Same chain as the "Auto (no clicks)" button of digitize_landmarks(), with the models loaded once (a fraction of a second per photograph on a CPU).

Usage

batch_landmarks(
  photos,
  out_dir,
  recursive = FALSE,
  qc = TRUE,
  open_qc = interactive(),
  max_fish = 1L,
  ruler = TRUE,
  ruler_mm = 10,
  min_bl_frac = 0.15,
  hinges = FALSE,
  redo = FALSE,
  mlmorph_dir = NULL,
  python = NULL
)

Arguments

photos

Folder of photographs, or a character vector of image paths.

out_dir

Output folder (created). A photograph already processed there is skipped unless redo = TRUE.

recursive

Look into sub-folders of photos.

qc

Write annotated thumbnails and a contact sheet qc/index.html, sorted by decreasing risk.

open_qc

Open the contact sheet in the browser when done.

max_fish

Fish per photograph. 1 (default): one fish, and a photograph carrying more is flagged plusieurs. More (plates): up to max_fish fish are found, numbered individual 1, 2, ... from top to bottom.

ruler

Do the photographs carry a ruler (scale bar)? TRUE (default): it is detected automatically (landmarks 20-21) and a photograph without a readable ruler is flagged règle. FALSE: no detection, no règle flag, measurements in pixels only. Applies to the whole call: run a folder with and a folder without ruler separately (a photograph already in out_dir keeps its first run unless redo = TRUE).

ruler_mm

Real distance between landmarks 20 and 21, in mm (used only when ruler = TRUE).

min_bl_frac

Flag threshold (see Details).

hinges

Also write the hinges 22/24 of the broken axis predicted by the model (curved fish). Off by default: away from the sites where hinges were clicked for training, predicted hinges bias the derived points.

redo

Process every photograph again.

mlmorph_dir, python

As in digitize_landmarks(): the ml-morph folder (NULL auto-detects it) and the Python interpreter (NULL: INTRAITR_MLMORPH_PY, ~/.venv_mlmorph/bin/python, then python3).

Value

Invisibly, a list: summary (one row per fish: photo, individual, ruler, dimensions, standard length in pixels bl_px, score, flags, risk, and with a ruler mm_per_px, bl_mm), landmarks (long: photo, individual, landmark, X, Y, conf) and out_dir.

Details

Nothing is written to the measurement journal: the result is a proposal to check. Every photograph gets quality flags and a risk score, so that only the doubtful ones need opening:

  • plusieurs: one fish more than max_fish was found (an undeclared plate);

  • dorsal: the dorsal side of the global network and the LM3 of the fine model contradict each other (fish possibly upside down);

  • petit: the fish spans less than min_bl_frac of the largest image side;

  • bord: a landmark within 1 percent of the image border;

  • confiance: score (mean confidence of the fine model) among the lowest 10 percent of the batch.

Localisation is robust to distractors (labels, reflections, other fish): several candidates are taken for the snout and the caudal base, and each snout-caudal pair is checked by the fine model, which recognises a real fish in the canonical frame; on plates, each fish found is masked before the next is searched.

Scale bar (20-21): when the photographs carry a ruler (ruler = TRUE, the default) and the ruler network mlmorph_run_ruler/model.onnx is present, the two graduations are located automatically and summary gains mm_per_px, scale_quality and bl_mm; a photograph whose ruler cannot be read is flagged règle, and one whose graduation period departs from the network's order of magnitude is flagged échelle. With ruler = FALSE nothing is searched and nothing is flagged: measurements stay in pixels. The choice is recorded per photograph in the ruler column of summary. Coordinates are in pixels of the raw pixel grid (EXIF orientation ignored, as in the applications).

See also

read_batch_landmarks(), digitize_landmarks()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- batch_landmarks("00_project/prepared/SAUDRUNE/20260427",
                       out_dir = "batch_saudrune", open_qc = TRUE)
subset(res$summary, flags != "")   # photographs to review
} # }
